sources.fact: University of Manchester, 'Human eggs prefer some men's sperm over others, research shows' (10 June 2020): human eggs release chemicals called chemoattractants that attract sperm to unfertilised eggs; researchers examined how sperm respond to follicular fluid, which surrounds eggs; follicular fluid from one female was better at attracting sperm from one male, while fluid from another female was better at attracting sperm from a different male; eggs did not always attract more sperm from their partner; published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B; Stockholm University and Manchester; research may eventually help understand some unexplained causes of infertility
EurekAlert (Stockholm University release), same study: different women's eggs attract different men's sperm, and not necessarily their partners'

News-Medical, 'The egg decides which sperm fertilizes it': researchers used follicular fluids and sperm from six couples undergoing infertility treatment; Proc. R. Soc. B. 287 20200805; Fitzpatrick: only a small fraction of sperm reach the egg

math.note: Fitzpatrick et al., Proc R Soc B 2020 (Manchester, June 2020)
News-Medical: follicular fluid and sperm from six couples

post.instagram_caption:
Human eggs might play favourites with sperm 🥚

An egg is surrounded by fluid that gives off chemicals that attract sperm. In a small 2020 lab study (6 couples), one woman's egg fluid pulled in one man's sperm best, while another woman's fluid preferred a different man. And it wasn't always her own partner.

Researchers hope this may one day help explain some unexplained infertility.

Sources: University of Manchester, Stockholm University via EurekAlert, News-Medical.

Did school ever tell you the egg might get a say?
